questions.question: In which kind of trigger can you modify the incoming row with `SET NEW.col = ...`?
questions.explanation: NEW is writable only in BEFORE triggers; AFTER triggers see final values, and DELETE has no NEW row at all.

questions.question: An UPDATE statement changes 10,000 rows in a table with an AFTER UPDATE trigger. How many times does the trigger body run?
options: 10,000 times, because MySQL triggers are row-level only
It depends on the ALGORITHM setting
questions.explanation: MySQL supports only FOR EACH ROW triggers, which is why heavy triggers make bulk operations slow.

questions.question: A parent row is deleted and `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes 5 child rows. Does a DELETE trigger on the child table fire?
options: Yes, once for the whole cascade
Only if the trigger is declared AFTER
No, foreign-key cascade actions do not fire triggers
questions.explanation: Cascaded foreign-key actions in InnoDB do not activate triggers, a classic reason audit triggers miss changes.

questions.question: What happens to a one-time event created with `ON SCHEDULE AT ...` after it runs, by default?
options: It is dropped, unless declared ON COMPLETION PRESERVE
questions.explanation: The default is ON COMPLETION NOT PRESERVE, so a finished one-time event is dropped automatically.
